steps.title: Sign in
steps.action: Enter your username, password and verification code. Click Sign In.
steps.note: Complete authenticator verification and any required password change when prompted.

steps.title: Open the registry
steps.action: Click Governance Hub, then API Client Registry.
steps.note: Check that the header shows Data Manager MODE.

steps.title: Check for an existing client
steps.action: Search for the application before creating another entry.
steps.note: If it already exists, select its row and jump to Query and Agent.

steps.title: Register the application
steps.action: Click Register New Client.

steps.title: Enter the approved name
steps.action: Fill Application Name and the approved outbound IP addresses.
steps.note: Use your actual application and IPs. Leave Client Public Key blank here; register it separately later.

steps.title: Save the new entry
steps.action: Click Confirm Registration and wait for the success message.
steps.note: Record the new client ID. The example address and application are demonstration data.

steps.title: Choose permitted reports
steps.action: On the intended client row, click Queries.

steps.title: Select an approved query
steps.action: Open Permitted Queries and select the approved Query Name.
steps.note: If missing, check Query Library → Approved. API Query Names cannot contain spaces.

steps.title: Save query access
steps.action: Click Save. Check the client’s authorized queries after refresh.

steps.title: Choose source nodes
steps.action: On the same client row, click Agents.

steps.title: Map the approved Agent
steps.action: Select the intended Agent. Click Update Node Scope.
steps.note: API-client Agent scope is separate from the API user’s subscription mapping.

steps.title: Review the calling IPs
steps.action: Click IP Whitelist on the client row.

steps.title: Save the IP policy
steps.action: Enter the approved calling IPs, then click Update Security Policy.
steps.note: Do not use the example IP. Do not clear restrictions just to make a test succeed.

steps.title: Check any required data segregation
steps.action: If the approval requires a response filter, click Segregation and save the approved field/value policy.
steps.note: Confirm the policy with the query owner. Also review the approved Status and Encryption settings.

steps.title: Open the version controls
steps.action: Click Guide / SDK / Test or Protocol versions.

steps.title: Choose the approved V2 row
steps.action: Find the query’s V2 / Signed freshness row. Click SDK.
steps.note: The version must be available, enabled and not retired. Save approved policy changes explicitly.

steps.title: Download the UAT files
steps.action: Click Download UAT SDK.
steps.note: Confirm this is the intended UAT client and gateway. This button does not create a new environment or key.

steps.title: Prepare the UAT identity
steps.action: Pause here. Check all five downloads and have the build custodian follow the UAT build README and run setup.
steps.note: Keep the files together. Resume when client_public.pem is ready. Full manual: pages 12–14.

steps.title: Open certificate registration
steps.action: Return to the same client row. Click Public Key.

steps.title: Load the public certificate
steps.action: Browse or drop client_public.pem in the public-certificate form.
steps.note: Use the setup-generated public certificate. Never upload the private P12 or wallet file.

steps.title: Inspect the certificate
steps.action: Click Analyze Content. Compare the displayed identity and fingerprint with the approved details.
steps.note: The illustration shows the form before a file is loaded; the button becomes available after loading public content.

steps.title: Register the matching public key
steps.action: After verifying the details, click Confirm & Save Key.
steps.note: Confirm you are changing the intended UAT client. Replacing a registered key can affect existing callers.

steps.title: Test and build the kit
steps.action: Pause here. Have the custodian make the approved UAT call, build the ZIP and verify its SHA-256 checksum.
steps.note: Use the generated setup/build instructions. Verify the data and each Agent’s result. Full manual: pages 16–17.

steps.title: Share the three release files
steps.action: Send the ZIP, readme-enduser-uat.txt and its .sha256 sidecar through the approved protected channel.
steps.note: Review the finalized doors-uat-mail.txt. Replace every placeholder, verify the secure link and obtain recipient acceptance. Full manual: page 18.

steps.title: Select the Production client
steps.action: After UAT acceptance, locate the separately approved Production client and open its Protocol versions.
steps.note: Confirm the Production key, gateway, query, Agent and IP policy before downloading.

steps.title: Select the Production query and V2
steps.action: On the intended query’s enabled V2 row, click SDK.

steps.title: Download Production files
steps.action: Click Download Production SDK.
steps.note: Keep all five files separate from UAT. The recipient owns its Production private identity.

steps.title: Prepare the Production release
steps.action: Pause here. Have the custodian follow the Production build README, run setup/build and verify the ZIP.
steps.note: The ZIP contains the API key, but must exclude the recipient’s private P12 and wallet. Full manual: page 19.

steps.title: Receive only the public certificate
steps.action: Ask the recipient to retain its private identity locally and supply only client_public.pem.
steps.note: Its PKI team must also prepare the approved TLS trust store. Full manual: page 20.

steps.title: Register the Production public key
steps.action: On the Production client, load the public certificate, Analyze Content, verify the fingerprint, then Confirm & Save Key.
steps.note: Do not replace another client’s certificate. Confirm registration with the recipient before its first call.

steps.title: Complete the Production handoff
steps.action: Share the verified ZIP, readme-enduser-prod.txt and .sha256 sidecar. Review doors-production-mail.txt and agree the first-call test.
steps.note: Replace the draft’s demo URLs with approved protected links. Record recipient acceptance. Full manual: pages 20–21.

steps.title: Map the API user
steps.action: Open API Subscriptions & Usage → Manage Agent mappings. Select the API user and its approved Agent.
steps.note: This controls subscriber service and usage attribution; source-Agent permissions remain in the API Client Registry.

steps.title: Save the service mapping
steps.action: Review the service state, then click Save Agent mapping & service.
steps.note: Changing service state can affect every API key under that Agent. Follow the approved subscription record.

steps.title: Save approved access hours
steps.action: On Weekly access, click Edit weekly access. Choose unrestricted or scheduled hours, then Save weekly access.
steps.note: Weekly slots use India time. A scheduled week with no slots blocks all hours. Existing date-specific restrictions also apply.

steps.title: Confirm the recipient can use the API
steps.action: Record the verified first call and acceptance. Monitor Usage & scorecards and any reported failures.
steps.note: The process is complete when the recipient confirms an authorized, verified result—not merely when the files download.
